message.content:
**Signatories of the United States Declaration of Independence**

When the Second Continental Congress adopted the text on **July 2, 1776**, it was later sent to the individual colonies for ratification. On **August 2–5, 1776**, representatives gathered in Philadelphia’s Pennsylvania State House (now known as Independence Hall) to formally endorse the document. A total of **56 delegates**—one per colony—signed the parchment. Below are the most widely recognized among them:

| Colony | Signer(s) |
|--------|-----------|
| Delaware | Richard Allen, Caesar Rodney |
| Georgia | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall |
| Connecticut | Roger Sherman, William Williams |
| Massachusetts | Joseph Hewes, Edward Rutledge |
| Maryland | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Daniel Carroll |
| New Hampshire | Josiah Bartlett, Matthew Thornton |
| New Jersey | Francis Hopkinson, John Hart |
| New York | Philip Livingston, Robert R. Livingston |
| North Carolina | Arthur Middleton, John Penn |
| South Carolina | Edward Tylor, William Hooper |
| Virginia | Edmund Randolph, George Wythe |
| Rhode Island | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery |

### Notable Figures Among Them  
- **John Hancock** – President of the Continental Congress, famously bold signature.  
- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal drafter of the Declaration.  
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned statesman and scientist.  
- **George Washington** – Commander-in-chief of the Continental Army.  
- **James Madison** – Future fourth U.S. President, influential legislator.  
- **Samuel Adams** – Revolutionary leader from Boston.  
- **Patrick Henry** – “Give me liberty!” speaker.  

These individuals, along with their fellow delegates, collectively affirmed the colonies’ intent to separate from Great Britain and establish an independent nation. For a complete roster of all 56 signers, you may consult resources such as the National Archives or reputable history websites dedicated to American founding documents.
